# Agent Instructions — Onnit

You can browse products and shop at Onnit's online store, https://www.onnit.com, on your user's behalf. This guide covers the Shop skill and UCP integration, directly or through browser-based WebMCP tools.

## Shop skill — recommended

Use the Shop skill to help your user shop with this store. Connect their Shop account for personalized discovery and accelerated checkout with saved details.

- Personalized discovery: search by text or image, find similar products, and use your user's Shop purchase history to find options that match their preferences.
- Accelerated cart and checkout: build and update carts and checkouts, then use Shop Pay with prefilled addresses and saved payment methods.
- Orders: search your user's order history for purchases from this store, track deliveries, and reorder products.

Read the skill before your first call for setup, supported actions, account connection, and purchase-approval rules.

## UCP integration

This store implements the Universal Commerce Protocol for product discovery, carts, and checkout. Integrate directly with its service, or orchestrate shopping through browser-based WebMCP tools.

### Direct integration (MCP)

1. Discover the store — `GET https://www.onnit.com/.well-known/ucp` returns its UCP profile, including capabilities, service endpoints, and payment handlers.
2. Discover available tools — Connect to the MCP endpoint advertised in the profile (`https://www.onnit.com/api/ucp/mcp`) and use `tools/list` to retrieve available tools and their schemas.
3. Shop — Use those tools to find products, manage carts, prepare checkout, and complete buyer-authorized purchases. Follow returned statuses, messages, and handoff URLs when buyer action is required.

Use a compatible UCP version and follow the returned tool schemas. For integration details, see Shopify's agent documentation.

### Browser integration (WebMCP)

When working through a browser, use the WebMCP tools registered on this store's pages. The checkout page exposes UCP tools over WebMCP. These tools act on the checkout in the current browser session.

- Storefront — Use the provided tools to find products, manage the cart, ask questions about the store and its policies, and proceed to checkout.
- Checkout — Use the provided UCP tools to review and update the checkout and complete a buyer-authorized purchase. Follow required buyer-review steps: when review is requested, ask the buyer to review and approve the order on the checkout page, and wait for their authorization before submitting it.

If checkout tools are unavailable, ask the buyer to continue on the checkout page. Do not fall back to scripted form fills or page controls.

For integration details, see Storefront WebMCP and Checkout WebMCP.

## Interaction guidelines

- Buyer authorization — Place orders and submit payment only with the buyer's authorization. Follow required review and approval steps.
- Agent traffic — Agents must identify their requests as agent-initiated. Server-to-server requests and hosted or remote browsers must use Web Bot Auth and follow the service's authentication requirements. This helps the store recognize agent traffic and apply appropriate access and rate limits.
- Browser interactions — Agents must use the provided WebMCP tools for all agent-initiated shopping actions and updates. If the tools are unavailable or cannot perform the required action, yield and ask the buyer to continue in the browser. Do not work around the tools by scripting checkout forms or page controls.
- Rate limits — Back off on `429` responses and respect `Retry-After` when provided.
- Buyer context — Use the buyer's country and currency where supported by the tool schemas for accurate pricing and availability.

## Read-only browsing

Prefer the structured information returned by the shopping tools described above. You may also read public HTML pages for additional context, provided your requests follow the agent-identification guidance

# Payment Methods at Onnit Updated 6 months ago

Here’s everything you need to know about paying for your purchase on Onnit.com:

### Accepted Payment Methods

We currently accept:

- Google Pay
- Credit Cards (excluding Mastercard for Free Trials)
- Debit Cards
- PayPal
- FSA/HSA through TruMed

### Not Accepted

- Split payments — We can only accept one payment method per order.

### Mastercard & Free Trials

Due to Mastercard’s restrictions, we cannot accept Mastercard for Free Trial offers. For other purchases, Mastercard is accepted.

### Tips for a Smooth Checkout

- Use a supported payment method listed above.
- Ensure your billing info matches your card details.
- If you run into issues, consider using PayPal for added flexibility.

- On-site

- Customer Success

## Job description

## About the Role

You're the person merchants call when their numbers don't add up. When a Shopify payout doesn't reconcile with the P&L, when COGS looks off, when a multi-currency gap shows up, you dig in, find the root cause, and walk the merchant through it. These are high-growth eCommerce brands selling across Shopify, Amazon, Walmart, and TikTok Shop. They use Fulfil as their ERP, and you're their first point of contact when something doesn't tie out.

You'll work with merchants ranging from D2C founders doing their own books to finance teams at 9-figure brands, both of whom need you to be sharp, clear, and confident on the call. Internally, you'll partner with our Engineering, Implementation, and Success teams in Bangalore.

If you thrive on variety, own problems end-to-end, and can explain a multi-currency FX discrepancy to a non-accountant in under two minutes, keep reading.

## About Fulfil

Fulfil is an ERP built for high-growth eCommerce brands. Our merchants run complex, multi-channel operations across Shopify, Amazon, Walmart, TikTok Shop, and beyond relying on Fulfil to keep their financials accurate, reconciled, and audit-ready.

## What You'll Actually Do

Day-to-day, you will:

- Own merchant accounting issues end-to-end: troubleshoot reconciliation discrepancies between Fulfil and sales channels like Shopify and Amazon, and walk merchants through exactly what went wrong and why
- Guide merchants on eCommerce accounting fundamentals: support merchants with COGS tracking, inventory valuation, revenue recognition, and multi-channel transaction reconciliation within Fulfil
- Implementation support: partner with the Implementation team on new merchant onboarding and advising on accounting workflow design, chart of accounts setup, and core financial configuration to ensure merchants go live on solid footing 
- Communicate clearly to diverse audiences: explain financial concepts to both technically savvy controllers and accountant-averse founders
- Support merchants through audits: help them pull the right documentation and reconciliations from Fulfil
- Advise on compliance and currency exposure: help merchants navigate sales tax across geographies (multiple US states, Canadian provinces, UK and others) and multi-currency accounting considerations
- Lead product adoption: identify where merchants are underutilizing Fulfil’s financial features, run targeted training session and consult on process improvements to drive longer-term value 
- Collaborate cross-functionally: surface recurring merchant pain points to Implementation, Support, and Engineering teams to shape product enhancements
- Leverage AI to move faster: use tools like Claude to clarify accounting treatments, compress context, or draft merchant updates

A realistic day might look like:

- Helping come up with a cutover plan for a merchant migrating from their current accounting software to Fulfil
- Helping a user troubleshoot and reconcile discrepancies within their ledger balances
- Conducting a training session with users, consulting and providing best practices
- Working closely with our product team by iterating on customer feedback

## Job requirements

## What We're Looking For

- 3+ years of accounting, audit, or finance-SaaS implementation/support experience — at an eCommerce company, a multi-client accounting BPO with eCommerce clients, a US/UK-focused accounting BPO, or as a functional/implementation consultant on a finance ERP 
- Hands-on working experience reconciling and closing books, not just familiarity
- Strong understanding of US GAAP and eCommerce-specific accounting: revenue recognition across channels, COGS, inventory valuation, and settlement reconciliation

Paired pulls in $3.6M to encourage more couples to get cosy with app-based relationship care | TechCrunch

# Paired pulls in $3.6M to encourage more couples to get cosy with app-based relationship care

 Natasha Lomas 

12:00 AM PDT · May 27, 2021

Can an app improve your romantic relationships? The founders behind Paired, a “relationship care” app for couples, believe it can. And since launching in October, with $1 million to kick things off, they’ve convinced 5,000+ coupled-up others to try their custom blend of partner quizzes, “relationship satisfaction” tracking, and audio tips from experts — to try to feel closer to their S.O.

Paired is now gunning for serious growth: It’s announcing $3.6 million in seed funding today, led by Eka Ventures with participation from existing investors including Taavet Hinrikus (Wise, formerly TransferWise), Harold Primat (investor and former professional racing driver), and the co-founders of Runtastic.

As part of the seed funding, Camilla Dolan of Eka Ventures will join the board alongside the app’s co-founders Kevin Shanahan and Diego López (who previously worked together at language learning app Memrise).

Paired says its goal for the new funding is to grow its user-base from 5,000+ to 100,000 over the next 18 months.

All sorts of audio-led wellness “self-care” apps have been bubbling up in recent years — offering individuals app-wrapped help with stuff like meditation and mindfulness; targeted motivation to combat anxiety and stress; or dishing up sex tips and sexual self-awareness.

Paired fits within that broader trend, albeit with a more explicit nudge to extend the self-care phenomenon to a unit of two romantically connected people.

As it looks for growth, the U.K.-based startup says it will continue to target the U.S., U.K., Canada and Australia, which are its main markets at this point. “We expect the growth to continue to come from here over the next 12 months,” says Shanahan.

“We’re building out our product team — hiring engineers, a product manager, a data scientist — to begin offering more varied and personalised relationship conversations for our users,” he goes on.

“Personalisation is a particular focus as every relationship is different and the app will begin to understand what your interests are, what stage you’re in, what would be most useful for you to discuss, etc. We’re also growing our content, working with new experts to cover more relationship topics and marketing the app via influencers, partnerships and other channels.”

Who are Paired’s early adopters? Currently, the average user is a straight, early 30s millennial who’s been in their current relationship for 2-3 years, according to Shanahan. (He says around 5% of users are LGBTQ+.)

But he also claims Paired has a wide mix of users, adding: “We have couples who have been together for 6 months and those who have been together for 10+ years, so it’s a wide spectrum.”

He says the split of women and men using the app is “fairly even” but avoids specifying exactly how usage splits on gender lines.

The app can be used by only one half of a couple — for solo relationship support/self-care, if preferred — but users have the option to pair with their partner to swap answers to relationship questions in order to encourage discussion. And that’s where Paired can offer the most personalized experience to users, by opening up a dedicated “relationship” discussion channel between the couple. (Paired does not obviously cater to open/polyamorous couples — but presumably could be used as a discussion tool for the primary partners.)

Search Kickoff Worksheet: A Completed Example — Paired Sourcing

# What a Completed Search Kickoff Worksheet Looks Like

 Nov 5 

Written by Paired Sourcing

Jer Langhans Founder, Paired Sourcing

A kickoff meeting can feel productive without giving anyone a clear direction for the search. The hiring manager wants someone strategic, hands-on, and comfortable with ambiguity. The recruiter takes good notes. Everyone leaves feeling aligned, until the first profiles arrive and it becomes clear that they were picturing different people.

The useful work happens when those broad descriptions turn into decisions. What does this person need to accomplish? Which capabilities have to be there on day one? Where might someone have done comparable work, even if their title or industry looks different?

Our Search Kickoff Worksheet puts those questions in one place. Here is what filling it out could look like, and how the answers would shape the research.

Illustrative example: The company, search, dates, and completed notes below are hypothetical.

## The search we are using

Imagine a B2B software company hiring a senior product marketing manager. The founder still carries too much of the sales story. Different salespeople explain the product differently, and marketing needs a clearer way to connect its capabilities to the problems buyers are trying to solve.

The job description starts with “strategic product marketer with SaaS experience.” That gives us a category. The worksheet needs to give us a direction.

> Role / team: Senior Product Marketing Manager / Marketing

> Hiring manager / recruiting contact / date: Head of Marketing / Internal recruiter / November 6, 2026

## 1. What must this person accomplish in their first 6 to 12 months?

> Example entry: Develop a clear positioning story grounded in customer and sales conversations. Use it to guide launch messaging and create sales materials that explain the business value without relying on the founder to translate.

Now we have something to research. We are looking for evidence that someone has understood buyers, made choices about positioning, and helped sales explain a product. A list of launches might be relevant, but it does not answer those questions by itself.

## 2. Which requirements are truly nonnegotiable?

> Example entry: Must have taken customer or prospect insights into a positioning or messaging decision, explained a complex product to business buyers, and worked directly with sales. Experience in our exact software category is a preference. Knowledge of our product can be learned.

This is where I would push on “SaaS experience.” Does the person need to understand a subscription business, a particular buyer, or a complex sales process? Those are different requirements. Naming the underlying capability gives the recruiter something more useful than a keyword to enforce.

## 3. What does an ideal candidate look like in the real world?

> Example entry: A product marketer who helped clarify the sales story for a complex B2B product. We would also consider someone from solutions consulting or sales enablement if they owned customer research and positioning decisions, beyond presenting materials someone else created.

The second background belongs in the research because the work might be comparable. It is still a hypothesis. A public profile may suggest relevant experience, while leaving ownership and depth unclear. Those become questions for the hiring team to assess, rather than assumptions we quietly treat as facts.

## 4. Where can we be flexible?

> Example entry: Open to adjacent B2B software categories and different current titles. Remote within the United States is workable. The approved compensation range still needs confirmation before outreach; record it as an open decision rather than guessing.

A useful worksheet can contain an unanswered question. The important part is making it visible and assigning someone to resolve it. Otherwise, the recruiter may spe

# How AI Is Changing Talent Sourcing

 Sep 27 

Written by Paired Sourcing

Every few months, someone declares that sourcing is dead.

Meanwhile, hiring teams still need help figuring out who to hire, where to look, and how to get the right people interested.

AI can help with research, search queries, outreach drafts, and organizing information. That gives sourcers more room for the work that requires judgment.

## Faster research still needs direction

A tool can produce a list. Someone still has to decide whether the search is asking the right question.

Does the hiring profile reflect the business need? Are we overlooking adjacent experience? What makes someone viable for this particular opportunity?

Those decisions shape the entire search.

## Hiring teams need market context

A useful sourcing partner helps hiring managers understand the market and adjust their assumptions. Finding profiles is one part of that relationship.

The conversations matter too: what candidates respond to, what concerns them, and what the team should learn from those responses.

Our sourcing process shows how that market intelligence, candidate outreach, and feedback fit together around a priority role.

## Where the opportunity is

The opportunity for sourcers is to bring stronger business understanding, clearer communication, and better judgment to increasingly capable tools.

Move faster. Stay thoughtful. Give the hiring team something useful to act on.

I explore a related question in If You Could Keep Only One Recruiting Tool, What Would It Be?: which part of the work do you actually need help with?

Which Recruiting Tool Would You Keep? — Paired Sourcing

# If You Could Keep Only One Recruiting Tool, What Would It Be?

 Oct 16 

Written by Paired Sourcing

If you could keep only one recruiting tool, what would you choose? LinkedIn is an obvious contender. Your ATS or CRM probably deserves a defense. AI belongs in the conversation, and so does the network you have spent years building. I think the interesting part is what each answer says about how you recruit.

After 25 years in sourcing, I care less about which tool wins the argument than which part of the work it helps someone do well. Finding people, remembering what you know about them, making sense of information and earning a conversation are different problems. A tool can be useful for one and leave you struggling with another.

## LinkedIn gives you a view of the market

For sourcing, visibility matters. You need a way to explore companies, follow career paths and start understanding where relevant experience might sit. LinkedIn can give you a useful starting point for that work, especially when you are learning a market you do not know well.

The judgment comes in deciding what that view tells you. A familiar title can hide very different work, and an unfamiliar title can hide exactly the experience you need. I want the research to go beyond matching words on a profile. What has this person actually done, and why might that matter for this role?

That is also why I would keep looking beyond LinkedIn for passive candidates. A view of the market is valuable. Knowing where that view is incomplete is part of the job.

## Your ATS or CRM preserves what you have learned

The case for an ATS or CRM is continuity. A recruiting team can put a lot of effort into a conversation, learn something useful and then struggle to find that context when a different role opens. The value is in being able to pick up the relationship with some understanding of what came before.

Useful notes might explain why the timing was wrong, what kind of work interested someone or what they needed to know before considering a move. That context gives the next conversation somewhere to start. It also depends on people recording information clearly and checking whether it is still relevant. Having a record and having a useful memory are two different levels of care.

## AI adds leverage to the work around a search

I see a place for AI in organizing research, exploring questions and helping develop a first pass that a person can examine. There is real value in having more room to think through a search instead of spending all your time assembling the inputs.

My standard is whether that help improves the next decision. I still want someone checking the underlying information, questioning an assumption and deciding whether an outreach message gives the recipient a reason to care. More output is useful when it makes the work better. It can also leave you with more material to review.

I explored that balance between faster research and human judgment in How AI Is Changing Talent Sourcing.

## A network brings context and trust

A network is the answer that makes this question harder, because it is built through the work itself. Conversations, introductions and the way you follow through all shape whether someone is willing to hear from you again. That history can give a conversation a different starting point from a cold approach.

I would still be careful about treating a network as complete coverage of a market. The people you already know can help you understand where to look, but a search may require experience outside those circles. Relationships and fresh research have room to support each other.

## Start with the part of recruiting that is getting stuck

If I were reviewing a recruiting team’s tools, I would start with a recent search and ask where progress slowed down. That makes the conversation more useful than a general debate about which platform deserves the budget.

# Paired Sourcing

Paired Sourcing is a Human Resources Services company. Paired Sourcing helps companies find and engage passive talent for hard-to-fill roles. They offer boutique sourcing built around their team and provide human-led sourcing with AI-enhanced tools. With 25 years of sourcing experience, they are paired with ambitious startup. Paired Sourcing employs 7 people (-12.5% YoY, -1 person), founded in 2015. Headquartered in Veradale, Washington, United States, with an office in Liberty Lake.

## About

Finding the people nobody else can.

Paired Sourcing helps companies find and engage passive talent for hard-to-fill roles. We work alongside internal recruiting and hiring teams, adding sourcing capacity without expanding the team.

Two ways to work with us: 
Sourcing Sprint — Focused research and proactive outreach for one priority role over 3–4 weeks. 
Sourcing Engine — An ongoing, embedded sourcing partnership supporting 1–3 priority roles, month to month.

We map the market, identify relevant people, and start thoughtful conversations. Your team gets market intelligence, a stronger candidate pipeline, and feedback that helps the search evolve.

Human judgment guides the work. Technology helps us move faster. Founded by Jer Langhans in 2015, Paired brings 25 years of sourcing experience to the searches that need a more thoughtful approach.

## Overview

The Director of Marketplaces for HEYDUDE will lead the end-to-end strategy and performance of the brand’s business across Amazon, Walmart, Target, and other major and emerging marketplace platforms. This consumer-focused and data-driven leader will be responsible for delivering a consistent brand experience from browse through fulfillment while driving customer acquisition, market share, category expansion, and profitable revenue growth. - Own the strategic vision and growth trajectory of the HEYDUDE marketplace business, driving market share gains, category expansion, customer acquisition, and profitable revenue growth across Amazon, Walmart, Target, and emerging platforms.

- Partner with merchandising and product teams to identify assortment gaps, establish launch priorities, and develop marketplace-exclusive opportunities that accelerate growth and increase market share.
- Partner with cross-functional teams to align marketplace strategies with key eCommerce initiatives, promotions, demand planning, brand marketing, and broader organizational priorities.
- Collaborate with the HEYDUDE Global eCommerce team to share marketplace insights and platform opportunities, establish brand-wide standards, and create a consistent consumer experience across channels.

## What You'll Bring to the Table

- Bachelor’s degree in business, marketing, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of relevant education and professional experience.

- Three to five years of experience leading and developing eCommerce talent, with a demonstrated ability to build high-performing teams and enable strong business results.
- Proven success leading businesses through significant scale, with experience managing a marketplace business of $100 million or more preferred.
- Demonstrated ability to develop annual marketplace strategic plans, budgets, and forecasts that align with departmental and organizational performance goals.

## About Nutrafol

Nutrafol is a health and wellness startup focused on addressing hair thinning and promoting hair growth through natural, drug-free supplements. The company operates in the consumer health and wellness market, specifically targeting individuals experiencing hair thinning and hair loss. Nutrafol's primary clients are both men and women who are concerned about hair health and are seeking effective, natural solutions.

The business model of Nutrafol revolves around selling its patented hair growth supplements directly to consumers through its website, nutrafol.com. These supplements are formulated with vitamins, minerals, and natural ingredients, and are designed to target the root causes of hair thinning, such as genetics, stress, diet, and exposure to toxins. Nutrafol's products are backed by clinical studies, ensuring that they are effective and safe for use.

Nutrafol makes money by selling its products online, offering personalized plans that are tailored to individual needs by naturopathic doctors. The company also collects consumer health data to better understand the needs of its customers and to improve its products and services. This data is used to provide personalized recommendations and to enhance the overall customer experience.

In summary, Nutrafol is a company dedicated to improving hair health through natural, clinically proven supplements. It serves a market of individuals concerned about hair thinning and hair loss, offering personalized, data-driven solutions to help them achieve visibly thicker and stronger hair.

Overview 

Manager Lease Accounting and Fixed Assets

 This is a hybrid role working Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday on-site reporting into the Support Center at Legacy West in Plano Texas

 About Sally Beauty Holdings, Inc.

At SBH, our purpose is to inspire a more colorful, confident, and welcoming world. We are the leader in professional hair color, selling and distributing professional beauty supplies across 11 countries through our Sally Beauty and Beauty Systems Group businesses. Sally Beauty offers products for hair color, hair care, nails, and skin care to retail customers looking for salon quality products at a value price. Beauty Systems Group, branded as Cosmo Prof or Armstrong McCall stores, along with its direct sales consultants, sell professionally branded products intended for use and resale by salons to retail consumers.

 About the Role

The Manager of Lease Accounting & Fixed Assets ensures the financial integrity of the company’s lease and asset portfolios. Key responsibilities include leading ASC 842 compliance, overseeing the fixed asset lifecycle (from CapEx to disposals), and applying GAAP expertise to technology and SaaS investments. Additionally, the role manages facilities-related expenses, strengthens SOX controls, and leads onshore/offshore teams to streamline month-end close and provide cross-functional financial insights.

Responsibilities

Oversee and verify the monthly rent run, ensuring all activity is complete, accurate, and compliant with underlying lease terms. Review and approve lease changes and inputs within Oracle to ensure accurate ASC 842 accounting and reporting.

- Oversee accounting and reporting for occupancy- and facilities-related expenses, including rent-related operating expenses, common area maintenance (CAM), utilities, and other facility costs, ensuring accurate accruals, classifications, and period recognition.
- Manage and review landlord payment activity, including reconciliation and approval of triple-net (NNN) charges. Ensure billings are compliant with lease terms and approve all adjustments to rent batches, including new and renewing store payments and escrow changes.
- Oversee the full fixed asset lifecycle, including capitalization, additions, transfers, disposals, and depreciation, ensuring compliance with Company policy and U.S. GAAP.
- Oversee accounting for cloud computing and SaaS arrangements, including evaluation of implementation costs, capitalization versus expense treatment, amortization, and ongoing expense recognition in accordance with U.S. GAAP and Company policy. Partner with IT and Technology teams to review contracts and project costs related to hosted and cloud-based systems.
- Prepare and/or review reconciliations, journal entries, roll-forward schedules, and supporting documentation for fixed assets, construction-in-progress, lease liabilities, SaaS-related balances, and occupancy-related accounts as part of the monthly close process.
- Ensure compliance with SOX requirements by identifying, assessing, and mitigating financial and operational risks. Maintain accurate and current process documentation and control narratives. Prepare annual lease obligation schedules and supporting documentation for inclusion in the Form 10-K.
- Lead and support special projects, including ad-hoc reporting, technical accounting analysis, process improvements, system enhancements, and other initiatives supporting Executive Management and broader Finance objectives.

Patrick Ta Beauty, founded in 2019, operates within the luxury color cosmetics market. The company was established through a collaboration between celebrated makeup artist Patrick Ta, product development specialist Rima Minasyan, and entrepreneur Avo Minasyan. Ta’s journey began after a failed nail and tanning salon venture, leading him to discover a passion for makeup at a MAC Cosmetics counter. He built his reputation and client base by showcasing his work on Instagram, eventually leading to high-profile collaborations with celebrities like Shay Mitchell and Gigi Hadid, which significantly elevated his career. This experience in professional artistry, coupled with a desire to create products he felt were missing from his kit, formed the foundation of the brand.

The business model combines direct-to-consumer sales through its website with strategic retail partnerships, most notably with Sephora, CULT Beauty, and Flannels Beauty. This multi-channel distribution strategy targets makeup enthusiasts who seek professional-quality products. The company generates revenue through the sale of its cosmetic products. In October 2022, Patrick Ta Beauty secured a minority growth investment from Stride Consumer Partners to support expansion and product innovation.

The product line is a direct reflection of Ta's signature artistry, which focuses on achieving a flawless, red-carpet-ready glow. A key feature of the brand is its dual-formula products, such as the iconic blush and contour duos that pair cream and powder in a single compact. This design is intended to make professional layering techniques accessible to a broader audience. The initial launch, named 'Major Glow,' featured highlighting mists, body oils, and lip shines designed to replicate Ta's sought-after dewy look. The portfolio has since expanded to a full suite of color cosmetics, including foundations, eyeshadow palettes, lipsticks, and various makeup tools, manufactured in locations like Italy, Korea, the US, and Japan.

Why Patrick Ta is heading to Latin America | Vogue

# Why Patrick Ta is heading to Latin America

The makeup artist-founded beauty brand has the bestselling blush line at Sephora. Now, to hit its growth goals, Ta and CEO Kimberly Villatoro are crossing a new market off its list.

By Hilary Milnes

August 27, 2025

Photo: Courtesy of Patrick Ta Beauty

Patrick Ta, the makeup artist-turned-influencer and founder, wants to build a global beauty brand that lasts. The next step towards that goal? Launching in Latin America.

Patrick Ta Beauty is entering the market with Sephora Mexico, going live on the Sephora app on 12 September before rolling out to 50 stores on 17 September. Ta will mark the launch with a three-day celebration, including a meet-and-greet at Sephora’s flagship in the Antara shopping mall in Mexico City, an influencer dinner with regional creators, and a makeup master class for local fans.

The move brings the beauty brand, launched in 2019 with co-founders Rima Minasyan and Avo Minasyan, to a market where Ta says it already has a fan base. A third of the brand’s audience identify as Latinx, according to a brand study. Ta says his approach is community first, having done some makeup classes in Mexico prior to entering the market. “We could gauge that we could pull a crowd and sell tickets. You need some recognition and in Mexico, the demand was always there,” says Ta.

Six years in, Patrick Ta Beauty has established itself as a breakout brand, becoming a top 15 seller at Sephora. (The brand declines to disclose sales but last year, estimates put it between £30-50 million.) After a minority investment from Stride Consumer Partners in 2022, Patrick Ta Beauty has distinguished itself from other beauty brands born from makeup artists and influencers, many of which prove to be flash in the pan.

Two and a half years ago, Ta brought on Kimberly Villatoro, a former Estée Lauder Companies (ELC) executive, as CEO to help formalise the business. The LA-based company now employs 40 people, and Villatoro has spent the last year-plus building up operations, including a robust supply chain and product pipeline. Adding global shipping last year gave a clearer picture of demand, Villatoro says, showing that Mexico was already the brand’s second biggest market after the US.

“Mexico is going to become one of our leading revenue-driving markets. It’s significant for us coming after a long period of focusing on the US and Canada,” says Villatoro, adding that the brand plans to expand to more markets outside of North America over the next three years. “We have big ambitions.”

The brand leaned on Sephora to help it determine how best to show up in the Mexican market, matching top performers by region in line with the brand’s product catalogue. Villatoro says it will start with its hero products first: blush, lip colour and foundation, which Ta launched last year.

Patrick Ta’s viral Double Take blush duos.

Photo: Courtesy of Patrick Ta Beauty.

As the brand moves into new markets, Ta also plans on expanding his product catalogue. He says customers can expect around four launches a year, and that the goal is to offer a “full face” in his collection.

“We don’t want to cannibalise what we have right now, but this industry is innovation driven and we’re all competing for the next best formula,” Ta says. “I want to be able to create a full Patrick Ta face.”

Correction: Kimberly Villatoro was hired two and a half years ago, not last year as previously reported. (2 September 2025)

# Patrick Ta Beauty has received a minority growth investment from Stride Consumer Partners

### Patrick Ta Beauty

Based in Los Angeles, California, Patrick Ta Beauty was founded in 2019 by world-renowned makeup artist to celebrities Patrick Ta, established product specialist Rima Minasyan and seasoned entrepreneur Avo Minasyan. Patrick Ta Beauty first launched with a range of mists and oils meant to deliver the camera-ready glow that Ta was known to create for celebrity clients, such as Gigi Hadid and Megan Fox, and has since expanded to include a full suite of color cosmetics and body products, including hyper-pigmented eyeshadows, blush, lipsticks, glosses and other makeup staples and tools. Patrick Ta Beauty is sold on its own direct-to-consumer website and in Sephora U.S. and internationally.

### The Deal

Lincoln International acted as the exclusive investment banking advisor to Patrick Ta Beauty, working closely with the owner-entrepreneur management team throughout the process. This transaction marks Lincoln’s first branded beauty deal under the direction of Ashleigh Barker, who leads the beauty practice at Lincoln International, and this transaction continues the firm’s impressive track record of working with owner-entrepreneurs. The minority growth investment is a demonstration of Lincoln’s commitment to extending its reputation for excellence into the beauty and personal care sector and is supported by recent execution banker hires at both the junior and senior levels with direct sector expertise to provide unmatched coverage for our clients.

“Lincoln’s hands-on approach allowed us to continue running our business without interruption from start to finish,” commented Co-founder Avo Minasyan, “and we look forward to partnering with Stride Consumer Partners through this exciting next phase of our growth.” Co-founder Patrick Ta added, “With this investment, Patrick Ta Beauty will be able to do more of what we have always done: make flawless red carpet looks, with the expertise of a makeup artist, easy to use and accessible to all skin tones and types.”

### Our Perspective

Ashleigh Barker, Director in Lincoln’s Consumer Group who leads the beauty practice, commented, “We believe Patrick Ta Beauty is well-positioned to continue its impressive growth in partnership with Stride, and we wish them continued success. The timing of this transaction is a strong indicator of investor confidence in the outlook of the beauty and personal care sector at large, especially for brands like Patrick Ta that are recognized for their incredible clean, inclusive beauty formulas designed to enhance and bring out one’s individual beauty. This is an area where the consumer has demonstrated a willingness to spend despite economic uncertainty time and time again, and today’s economic environment is no exception.”

Christopher D. Petrossian, Managing Director and co-head of Lincoln’s U.S. Consumer Group, stated, “Leading, entrepreneur-led brands such as Patrick Ta continue to attract strong interest from domestic and international strategic and financial investors.
